RoomType.maps_to: driver.py's Event fight path (`_run_event`) always calls `_run_combat(event.pending_encounter, RoomType.MONSTER)`, matching PunchOffEventEncounter.cs:9's `RoomType.Monster`. PunchOff is a Combat-layout event (`is_combat_layout=True`, punch_off.py:68-69): the encounter is generated at ROOM ENTRY via `_combat_layout.pregenerate_monster_hp`, mirroring `EventRoom.EnterInternal`/`GenerateInternalCombatState` (EventModel.cs:383-403); FIGHT reuses that state (`internal_combat_encounter`) rather than generating a second one, mirroring `EnterCombatWithoutExitingEvent`'s `ShouldCreateCombat = LayoutType != Combat` guard (EventModel.cs:624-628). Constructed once per room-visit, not re-seeded on FIGHT -- confirmed by reading `_fight`/`internal_combat_encounter` (punch_off.py:99-103, events/base.py:190-199).

AllPossibleMonsters.maps_to: no explicit sim field (whole-tree grep is empty, see battleworn_dummy_event); `_PunchOffEncounter.monster_classes = [PunchConstruct, PunchConstruct]` already equals the C# superset `{PunchConstruct}` (PunchOffEventEncounter.cs:11) exactly.
AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: No sim representation of the concept, but the fixed 2-of-one-class roster IS its own superset here, so nothing is lost.

GenerateMonsters.maps_to: `_PunchOffEncounter.create_monsters` (punch_off.py:26-40). Roster/order: 2 PunchConstructs, the FIRST built with `starts_with_fast_punch=True`, matching PunchOffEventEncounter.cs:15-19's construction order (the left construct gets `StartsWithFastPunch = true` first, the second does not). Draw count: 2 -- one `NextInt(2,10)` per construct, matching PunchOffEventEncounter.cs:17,19's two `base.Rng.NextInt(2, 10)` calls exactly (count AND per-construct order: construct 1's draw happens before construct 2's, on both sides). Draw VALUE: WRONG in parity mode -- see the `_entry_slug_mismatch` guard below, which is LIVE for this unit specifically because this is the only one of this batch's five GenerateMonsters bodies that actually consumes its per-encounter Rng. In LEGACY mode (no `rng_set`), `create_monsters` falls back to `rng.randint(2, 9)` on the shared per-combat `random.Random` whenever `selection_rng is None` (punch_off.py:37-38) -- this is the SAME shape already named `encounter/_selection_rng_fallback` by a sibling batch's `flyconid`/`two_tailed_rats` findings (matched here under Rule 3, not re-derived): the roster draw is not independent of the run's other draws in that configuration, breaking `EncounterModel.Rng`'s documented independence guarantee (EncounterModel.cs:42-49). See guard G2.
GenerateMonsters.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). `Encounter` gained an explicit `entry_slug` field and `Encounter.entry` returns it when set, so this unit seeds `make_encounter_rng` with the game's real `ModelId.Entry` while keeping its sim id. A mechanical sweep of ALL 87 sim encounters against `src/Core/Models/Encounters/*.cs` (audit/tools/encounter_entry_sweep.py) found two more the unit batches had not checked — `fuzzy_wurm_crawler` (FuzzyWurmCrawlerWeak) and `overgrowth_crawlers_normal` (OvergrowthCrawlers) — and now reports MATCH for every one. Pinned by test/test_encounter_entry_slugs.py.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: encounter/_entry_slug_mismatch (see G1): the wrong per-encounter Rng seed produces the wrong `StartingHpReduction` for BOTH Punch Constructs at a given run seed/floor. Executed: `py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e9.py punch-off-wrong-seed` -- at run_seed=12345, floor=7, the sim's actual (wrong) seed rolls `[2, 4]` and the game's real seed rolls `[5, 7]`; DIVERGENT=True. `PunchConstruct.adjust_hp_after_added` (punch_construct.py:50-61) spends this value as `max(1, hp - reduction)` on the CURRENT HP only, matching `PunchConstruct.AfterAddedToRoom` (PunchConstruct.cs:71-79) exactly in mechanism -- the divergence is entirely in the input value, not in how it is applied. This is an observable, in-game HP difference on both fighters of a real, reachable event fight (PunchOff.IsAllowed only requires TotalFloor >= 6).

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.maps_to: EncounterModel.ShouldReceiveCombatHooks => false (EncounterModel.cs:39, inherited, not re-overridden). The sim never registers an Encounter as a hook listener anywhere (checked every `hooks.register(` call site in the repo).

guards.what: encounter/_entry_slug_mismatch: `_PunchOffEncounter.entry` = `PUNCH_OFF_EVENT` (from `id="punch_off_event"`), but the game's real `Id.Entry` for `PunchOffEventEncounter` is `PUNCH_OFF_EVENT_ENCOUNTER` (`StringHelper.Slugify(type.Name)` via `ModelDb.GetEntry`) -- the sim's id drops the '_ENCOUNTER' suffix. This is fed to `rng.make_encounter_rng(seed, floor, entry)` both at room entry (`_combat_layout.pregenerate_monster_hp`) and again when the real fight is built (`RunState.create_combat`'s `encounter_selection_rng`) -- both call sites use `encounter.entry`, so both are equally wrong, consistently (the sim's own internal consistency is why the two calls still agree with EACH OTHER; they just no longer agree with the game). `make_encounter_rng`'s FORMULA is independently verified faithful (`seam/rng_streams` step 21); this finding is that the KEY fed into that correct formula is wrong for all 5 of this batch's units. Executed: `py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e9.py entry-slug-mismatch` prints MISMATCH; `py audit/tools/encounter_probes_e9.py punch-off-wrong-seed` demonstrates the resulting value divergence.

A mechanical sweep of ALL 87 sim encounters against `src/Core/Models/Encounters/*.cs` (audit/tools/encounter_entry_sweep.py) found two more the unit batches had not checked — `fuzzy_wurm_crawler` (FuzzyWurmCrawlerWeak) and `overgrowth_crawlers_normal` (OvergrowthCrawlers) — and now reports MATCH for every one. Pinned by test/test_encounter_entry_slugs.py.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: Cross-referenced from the GenerateMonsters hook above (this is the same mechanism; recorded once as a guard because it is a wiring defect in how the Rng is SEEDED, not in GenerateMonsters' own draw count/order, which are both correct). LIVE for this unit -- the only one of this batch's five whose GenerateMonsters actually draws from the resulting Rng. Also filed dormant (same mechanism id, live:false) on `battleworn_dummy_event/G1`, `dense_vegetation_event/G1`, `fake_merchant_event/G1` and `mysterious_knight_event/G1` -- those four units build the same kind of mis-seeded Rng but never draw from it.

guards.what: encounter/_selection_rng_fallback (matched under Rule 3 from a sibling batch's `flyconid`/`two_tailed_rats` findings, not re-derived here): in LEGACY mode (`RunState.rng_set is None`, the RL training/eval path -- `run_env.py` never passes a `string_seed`), `RunState.create_combat` USED TO pass `encounter_selection_rng=None` (historically run.py:1609-1613, pre-fix), and `_PunchOffEncounter.create_monsters` (punch_off.py:36-38) fell back to `rng.randint(2, 9)` on the SAME shared per-combat `random.Random` every other unseeded draw in the fight uses -- not an isolated stream. `EncounterModel.Rng`'s own doc comment (EncounterModel.cs:42-49) says this independence is exactly the point ("safe... because we don't need to keep track of a given encounter's RNG state once it's over") -- false in that configuration, since the draw shared state with, and could desync, every other draw in the same combat. Now superseded -- see the CLOSED rationale below; `run.py:1702-1706` builds an independent `encounter_selection_rng` unconditionally.
guards.rationale:
CLOSED 2026-08-03 (gap-fix pass). `RunState.create_combat` now builds the per-encounter Rng on BOTH paths: with a string seed from `rng_set.seed` as before, and without one from a run seed derived at construction (`run.derive_encounter_seed`, a hash of the shared generator's STATE, so it consumes no draw and shifts no other legacy stream). `create_monsters`' `selection_rng=None` arm is therefore unreachable from any production call site, and the composition no longer moves when the shared stream does — executed in test/test_encounter_selection_rng.py (test_the_composition_does_not_move_with_the_shared_stream) and by audit/tools/encounter_probes_e2.py legacy-shared-stream.

WHAT THE GAP SAID: Same family as flyconid/G1 (batch e1) and two_tailed_rats/G2 (batch e8) -- the LEGACY-mode `selection_rng is None` fallback loses `EncounterModel.Rng`'s documented independence for every encounter that draws in `create_monsters`, this one included. Not re-verdicted from scratch: matched under Rule 3 to the family those batches named. The PARITY path (`rng_set` set) is unaffected by THIS particular mechanism (it correctly threads an independent `make_encounter_rng`-seeded stream) -- see G1 above for parity mode's own, separate defect.
